correctness.rationale: Each valid confluence is uniquely oriented toward the root after one edge deletion. Cut j requires the prefix before j to increase and the suffix after j to decrease. Two cuts at distance at least three impose opposite inequalities on a shared pair. Adjacent cuts have binomial(n,j) common orders; distance-two cuts have binomial(n-1,j), all satisfying the middle cut as well. Summing single, pair, and triple incidences gives n*2^(n-1), 3*2^(n-1)-4, and 2^(n-1)-2; inversion gives all four claimed bins. The two monotone orders exhaust the second bin of positive multiplicities, and the triples are exactly the strict interior-peak unimodal orders. The factorial denominator implies decay faster than any fixed geometric rate. The temporal-election embedding represents all n cycle voters; the extra abstainer is not counted and has no path to the casting sink.
residual_risks: The supplied checker is finite corroboration for n=3 through 8; the unrestricted theorem rests on the incidence proof.
Uniformity is over permutations of distinct times, not a sampling law over spanning trees or tied times.

value.rationale: The rooted cycle is a natural first network with competing spanning routes. The exact law quantifies both strict scarcity of feasible trees and the exceptional orders allowing several choices, rather than merely counting individual paths or reporting the mean. It provides an exact baseline for reliability of full representation under random one-shot approvals.
